question: Can a tiny local task list preserve acknowledged tasks and make repeated create requests safe across fresh processes?
hypothesis: The SQLite implementation passes every declared claim with nonzero exercise counts. Deliberately volatile and duplicate-accepting implementations are rejected for the defects they contain.

claims.restart: An acknowledged task is visible unchanged to a fresh process.
claims.retry: An identical request ID and title return the same task, including after an ignored successful response and across eight concurrent processes.
claims.conflict: Reusing a request ID with a different title fails without changing the saved task.
claims.validation: An empty title fails without adding a task.

disconfirming: Any acknowledged task disappears in a fresh process
A retry creates another task or changes its identity
Any required exercise count is zero
Either deliberately broken implementation passes its targeted claim
The same deterministic scenarios disagree between independent repeats
scope: Local process boundaries and SQLite commits only. No power-loss, filesystem-failure, throughput, security or AI-model-quality claim.
